Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Football | National FIFA immortalises Caleb Yirenkyi’s torn Black Stars jersey at World Cup museum Source : Joy Sports 17 November 2026 8:39am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
FIFA has immortalised Caleb Yirenkyi’s torn Black Stars jersey from the 2026 FIFA World Cup, preserving a piece of Ghanaian football history at its museum in Zurich, Switzerland.
The jersey was damaged during Ghana’s opening match against Panama, in which the midfielder scored a dramatic last-minute winner to secure a 1-0 victory.
Yirenkyi’s match-worn shirt is expected to become part of the FIFA Museum’s permanent collection, where it will be preserved for historical purposes and future generations.
The gesture recognises a memorable moment from Ghana’s campaign at the first 48-team edition of the World Cup.
OFFICIAL: FIFA Museum has immortalized Caleb Yirenkyi’s Black Stars kit which got ripped off during the World Cup in North America. The World Football Governing body has kept the shirt in a special wardrobe for Historic reasons as it also serves as a one of the monumental factors which will remind the world about its first ever 48-team World Cup campaign.
The jersey also joins other significant football memorabilia, including the shirt worn by former Black Stars captain Asamoah Gyan during Ghana’s 2010 World Cup campaign in South Africa.
Gyan’s jersey documents one of the most heartbreaking moments in Ghanaian football history, when he missed a last-minute penalty against Uruguay in the quarter-finals before the Black Stars lost in the subsequent shootout.
The Black Stars finished third in Group L with four points after a 1–0 win over Panama, a goalless draw with England and a defeat in their final group game.
Ghana’s campaign ended on July 4 in Kansas City following a narrow 1–0 Round of 32 loss to Colombia, with Jhon Arias scoring the winner in the 14th minute.
The Black Stars finished as Africa’s fifth-best team, recording one win, one draw and two defeats.
